heading: Moving role types and compiler checks
body: A type that has a role cannot stay inline in a controller file or in a Tac service. For each role type, do these steps. Rename it. Update the typed dependency fields, or the lowerCamel field names in JavaScript. Update any Named provider names, Store entity classes and behavior factory references. Move the type into the matching shared plural role folder of its realm. Controllers go in server/controllers. Remove old module manifests. The compiler works on an immutable snapshot (a copy of the files that does not change). It checks the original source paths before annotation lowering, the step that turns annotations into ordinary code. Missing files, wrong languages or realms, unsafe paths, duplicate declarations, conflicting roles and invalid names fail closed: the compiler rejects them. Only files with a role annotation register, within their entry scope. Helpers without annotations do not register, and there is no global DI (dependency injection) container. In Yon, an included role file may not use a relative import (`TY2101`); standard-library imports and realm-root imports such as `/models/Guide.ts` are allowed. A Tac JavaScript or TypeScript file may import a file of its own realm with a relative path, and no file may import a file of the other realm (`TY1369`). Annotations need no import. Helpers without annotations keep the ordinary rules of their language. Existing per-invocation scopes, ownership that you state in code and adapter authorization do not change.
